title: Godzilla Stars Bring Hollywood Cheers Back to Tokyo
summary:
Fans were shouting the director's name like a rock star's.

At the 39th Tokyo International Film Festival on Sunday, the stars of Godzilla Minus Zero relived the film's premiere in Los Angeles, two days before the new movie opens in Japan. Kamiki Ryunosuke returns as Shikishima Koichi, and Hamabe Minami returns as his wife Noriko. Both had flown back to Japan only two days earlier from the premiere at the TCL Chinese Theatre.

Kamiki said the energy was extraordinary and that feeling the enthusiasm firsthand reminded him how deeply Godzilla is loved around the world. Applause in the 900-seat theater reportedly continued without a break. Some fans wore Godzilla-themed outfits or badges, held large posters, and asked for autographs. When director Yamazaki Takashi went to sign, the crowd erupted again, with chants of 'TAKASHI!' from the red carpet, which was open to passersby.

The Tokyo event was also the first stage appearance of child actor Nagatani Sae, who returns as Akiko. In Godzilla Minus One, she was very young and her part was mostly crying or single words. This time, Kamiki said, she had memorized full dialogue perfectly. Hamabe said Nagatani had grown into a dependable young actor who chatted with them and taught them things.

According to Kamiki, the new story picks up about two years after Minus One, while Hamabe put the gap at two to three years. The family has settled into everyday life before Godzilla resurfaces.

Minus One grossed more than 7.65 billion yen, or $50 million, in Japan, won the visual effects prize at the Oscars, and collected more than 50 honors. Minus Zero is described as the first Japanese film certified as Filmed for Imax.
why_it_matters: The event shows how a Japanese film series can excite fans in different countries at the same time. It also highlights the success of Minus One, which earned major honors before this follow-up.
